newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwanda says U.N. Zaire resolution "absurd".
newsitem.headline: Rwanda says U.N. Zaire resolution "absurd".

text.p: Rwanda said on Wednesday a U.N. Security Council resolution calling for a truce in the war in Zaire was "absurd" because it failed to take into account rebel views.
Burundi welcomed the five-point U.N. peace plan but, like Rwanda and Uganda, again rejected Zairean government accusations that their troops were fighting alongside the Zaire rebels.
"They (Security Council) are starting on the wrong footing," Claude Dusaidi, political adviser to Rwandan strongman Vice-President and Defence Minister Major-General Paul Kagame, told Reuters.
"They gave proposals without consulting the other party (rebels) in the conflict," he said by telephone from Kigali.
"This is clearly absurd because even if neighbours like us agree to the proposals, they would be useless without the agreement or consent of the rebel group," he added.

In Burundi's capital, Information Minister Pierre-Claver Ndayicariye told Reuters: "Burundi is not involved in the crisis in Zaire, but we will support any and all initiatives which could restore peace and security in the region."
Zaire criticised the resolution as "too timid" for not condemning the alleged intervention of its neighbours in the fighting.

Dusaidi said Rwanda would support a resolution calling for an immediate ceasefire and direct talks between the Zairean government and rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL).
Tuesday's Security Council resolution called for an immediate ceasefire but spoke only of a peaceful settlement of the crisis through dialogue and convening of an international conference.

"The Security Council should call for a ceasefire and direct talks between the two sides in the conflict. If you ignore the rebels and talk only to Kinshasa and the neighbours then you achieve nothing," Dusaidi said.
Rebels led by Laurent Kabila have seized a stretch of eastern Zaire at least 1,000-km (600 miles) long bordering on Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi and Tanzania since the start of their revolt in October.
Dusaidi criticised U.N. and Organisation of African Unity (OAU) Special Envoy Mohamed Sahnoun for sending recommendations to the Security Council without consulting all parties to the conflict.
The Security Council resolution followed a request from Sahnoun, who arrived in Kigali on Wednesday from Kinshasa. He is not known to have had any contact with the rebels.
"He acted prematurely. He should have first finished consulting everyone in the region, especially the parties to the conflict, before making the proposals," Dusaidi said.

The Security Council plan envisaged an immediate ceasefire, withdrawal of all foreign forces, including mercenaries, and respect for the national sovereignty and territorial integrity of Zaire and other states in the region.
Zairean Foreign Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda said the Security Council should consider Zaire's demand for a "global and unequivocal resolution on the aggression of which east Zaire is the target".
